description: An early large-scale text-to-image model demonstrating that autoregressive Transformer modeling could generate images conditioned on natural language.

name: DALL·E 2
description: A major transition in the DALL·E lineage toward diffusion-based image generation with CLIP-based semantic conditioning.

name: DALL·E 3
description: A later DALL·E generation focused on improved prompt following, compositional understanding, and natural-language-controlled image generation.

name: S4
description: Structured State Space Sequence models introduced a scalable formulation of continuous-time state-space models for long-range sequence modeling.

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

name: S5
description: Simplified State Space Layers reformulated S4 into a single multi-input multi-output state-space layer while retaining efficient long-range sequence modeling.

sources.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling

name: Mamba
description: Mamba introduced selective state spaces whose parameters depend on the input, providing content-aware sequence processing without conventional attention and with linear scaling in sequence length.

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

name: Mamba-2
description: Mamba-2 introduced the State Space Duality framework, connecting structured state-space models with attention-like computations and producing a faster simplified selective SSM.

name: Mamba-3
description: A later Mamba research generation exploring improved state-space formulations, complex-valued dynamics, and stronger long-context language modeling.

name: RWKV
description: RWKV combines Transformer-like channel mixing with recurrent time mixing, providing parallelizable training and recurrent inference without conventional quadratic attention.

sources.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

name: RWKV-5
description: RWKV-5 introduced matrix-valued states and improved recurrent time mixing, providing greater representational capacity while retaining efficient recurrent inference.

name: RWKV-6
description: RWKV-6, also known as Finch, introduced dynamic recurrence mechanisms that make the recurrent state update depend more flexibly on the current input.

name: RWKV-7
description: RWKV-7, codenamed Goose, introduces generalized dynamic state evolution and moves beyond earlier attention/linear-attention formulations.

sources.title: RWKV-7 Goose with Expressive Dynamic State Evolution

name: Hyena
description: Hyena is a subquadratic sequence operator replacing attention with implicitly parameterized long convolutions and data-controlled gating.

name: HyenaDNA
description: A genomic foundation model using Hyena operators to model DNA sequences at single-nucleotide resolution with very long contexts.

name: RetNet
description: Retentive Network replaces standard attention with a retention mechanism that supports parallel training, recurrent inference, and chunkwise recurrent computation.

name: xLSTM
description: Extended Long Short-Term Memory revisits recurrent neural networks with exponential gating and matrix-valued memory, creating a modern recurrent architecture capable of scaling to language-model workloads.

name: Linear Attention
description: A broad class of attention alternatives that restructure attention computation to avoid explicitly materializing the full quadratic token-to-token attention matrix.

name: Gated DeltaNet
description: A gated delta-rule sequence architecture combining linear-attention state updates with selective forgetting and input-dependent memory modification.

name: Titans
description: Titans introduces a neural long-term memory that learns during inference and combines it with short-term attention to model very long contexts.

sources.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

name: BitNet
description: BitNet explores replacing conventional dense floating-point weights with extremely low-bit representations, targeting substantial reductions in memory, energy, and computation.

name: BitNet b1.58
description: BitNet b1.58 extends the 1-bit idea to ternary weights {-1, 0, +1}, aiming to preserve model capability while dramatically reducing arithmetic and memory requirements.

name: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts
description: A foundational sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture in which a learned gating network routes each token to a small subset of specialized expert networks, allowing parameter count to grow without proportionally increasing computation per token.

sources.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

name: Switch Transformer
description: Switch Transformer simplified Mixture-of-Experts routing by sending each token to a single expert, enabling very large parameter counts while maintaining relatively low computational cost per token.

scale.activeParameters: single expert plus shared Transformer components

sources.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

name: GLaM
description: GLaM is a large sparse language model using Mixture-of-Experts layers to increase total parameter capacity while activating only a fraction of parameters for each token.

sources.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

name: Mixtral
description: Mixtral applies sparse Mixture-of-Experts routing to a modern decoder-only Transformer, with each token routed to a small number of experts while retaining a large total parameter capacity.

name: Mixtral 8x7B
description: An 8-expert sparse decoder-only Transformer in which two experts are selected for each token.

name: Mixtral 8x22B
description: A larger Mixtral generation using eight experts and activating two experts per token to provide substantially higher total model capacity.

name: DBRX
description: DBRX is an open-weight decoder-only language model using a fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts architecture with many smaller experts and top-k routing.

name: DeepSeekMoE
description: DeepSeekMoE introduced fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts, allowing specialized experts to model different knowledge while shared experts capture common knowledge.

sources.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

name: DeepSeek-V2
description: DeepSeek-V2 combines fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts with Multi-head Latent Attention, substantially reducing inference cost while maintaining high total parameter capacity.

name: DeepSeek-V3
description: DeepSeek-V3 is a large-scale MoE language model combining fine-grained routed experts, shared experts, Multi-head Latent Attention, and auxiliary-loss-free load balancing.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: shared + routed experts with dynamic load balancing

name: Jamba
description: Jamba combines Mamba State Space layers, Transformer attention, and Mixture-of-Experts layers in a single architecture, demonstrating a hybrid route beyond pure Transformer designs.

name: Qwen MoE
description: The Qwen family includes sparse Mixture-of-Experts variants designed to increase total model capacity while limiting the number of active parameters for each token.

name: Mixture-of-Depths
description: Mixture-of-Depths dynamically allocates a fixed computation budget by routing only selected tokens through expensive Transformer blocks while allowing others to bypass them.

sources.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in Transformer-based language models

name: Multi-Head Attention
description: The standard Transformer attention mechanism in which multiple attention heads independently project queries, keys, and values, allowing different heads to model different relationships.

name: Multi-Query Attention
description: Multi-Query Attention shares a single key and value head across all query heads, dramatically reducing KV-cache memory during autoregressive decoding.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: multiple query heads with shared K/V

sources.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

name: Grouped-Query Attention
description: Grouped-Query Attention divides query heads into groups that share key and value heads, providing a middle ground between the expressive capacity of MHA and the KV-cache efficiency of MQA.

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints

name: Multi-Head Latent Attention
description: Multi-Head Latent Attention compresses key-value representations into a shared low-dimensional latent representation for efficient KV caching while retaining multi-head expressive capacity.

name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
description: The original Transformer positional encoding represents token positions using deterministic sine and cosine functions added to token representations.

name: RoPE
description: Rotary Position Embedding injects position information by rotating query and key representations according to their token positions, naturally encoding relative positional relationships.

sources.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding

name: ALiBi
description: ALiBi adds position-dependent linear biases directly to attention scores instead of adding explicit positional embeddings.

name: YaRN
description: YaRN provides an efficient method for extending the context window of RoPE-based Transformer models using frequency-aware interpolation and attention-temperature scaling.

sources.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

name: LongRoPE
description: LongRoPE extends RoPE-based context windows through non-uniform positional interpolation and evolutionary search over positional scaling factors.

sources.title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens

name: Sliding Window Attention
description: Sliding Window Attention restricts each token's attention to a local neighborhood, reducing attention computation while allowing information to propagate across layers.

name: Longformer
description: Longformer combines local sliding-window attention with selected global attention positions to efficiently process long documents.

name: BigBird
description: BigBird combines local attention, random attention, and global attention to reduce the quadratic complexity of full attention while preserving important long-range interactions.

sources.title: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences

name: FlashAttention
description: FlashAttention is an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that reduces high-bandwidth-memory reads and writes through tiling and kernel-level optimization without approximating the attention result.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

name: FlashAttention-2
description: FlashAttention-2 improves GPU work partitioning and parallelism over FlashAttention, substantially increasing attention throughput while retaining exact attention.

sources.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning

name: Ring Attention
description: Ring Attention distributes long sequences across multiple devices and circulates key-value blocks around a ring, enabling attention over contexts larger than the memory of a single accelerator.

scale.parameters: does not fundamentally change parameter count

sources.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context

name: Native Sparse Attention
organization: DeepSeek / Peking University / University of Washington
description: Native Sparse Attention is a trainable sparse attention mechanism using a hierarchical strategy that combines coarse-grained token compression with fine-grained token selection while co-designing the algorithm with modern hardware.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: compressed global view + selected fine-grained tokens

sources.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention

name: Byte Pair Encoding
description: Byte Pair Encoding iteratively merges frequent symbol pairs to construct a vocabulary of subword units. It became one of the dominant tokenization approaches for neural language models.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

name: WordPiece
description: WordPiece constructs a subword vocabulary using a likelihood-oriented vocabulary selection strategy and became strongly associated with BERT-family models.

name: SentencePiece
description: SentencePiece is a language-independent subword tokenizer framework that learns directly from raw text without requiring pre-tokenized word boundaries.

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing

name: Unigram Language Model Tokenization
description: The Unigram tokenizer treats tokenization as a probabilistic segmentation problem and iteratively removes vocabulary pieces while minimizing corpus likelihood loss.

sources.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates

name: Byte-Level BPE
description: Byte-Level BPE applies BPE over byte representations rather than Unicode characters, allowing a tokenizer to represent arbitrary text and reducing unknown-token problems.

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

name: tiktoken
description: A fast tokenizer implementation used by OpenAI model families, implementing byte-pair encoding and model-specific vocabularies.

name: ByT5
description: ByT5 removes the conventional subword tokenizer and operates directly on UTF-8 bytes, allowing the model to handle arbitrary text and noisy inputs without vocabulary-based tokenization.

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

name: CANINE
description: CANINE operates directly on characters rather than subword tokens, using downsampling and Transformer processing to make character-level modeling computationally practical.

sources.title: CANINE: Pre-training an Efficient Tokenization-Free Encoder for Language Representation

name: Charformer
description: Charformer learns latent subword-like representations directly from character sequences using a fast soft tokenization mechanism, avoiding a fixed external tokenizer.

sources.title: Charformer: Fast Character Transformers via Gradient-based Subword Tokenization

name: MegaByte
description: MegaByte performs autoregressive modeling directly over bytes using a multi-scale architecture that separates local byte modeling from longer-range patch modeling.

sources.title: MegaByte: Predicting Million-byte Sequences with Multiscale Transformers

name: Llama SentencePiece Tokenization
description: The Llama family uses a SentencePiece-based subword tokenizer with byte fallback, providing a robust multilingual text representation for decoder-only Transformer models.

name: ViT Patch Embedding
description: Vision Transformer represents an image as a sequence of fixed-size image patches that are projected into token embeddings and processed by a Transformer.

name: VQ-VAE
description: VQ-VAE learns a discrete latent representation using vector quantization, creating a codebook of learned representations that can turn continuous inputs such as images into discrete latent tokens.

name: VQGAN
description: VQGAN combines vector-quantized latent representations with adversarial and perceptual objectives to learn compact high-quality discrete image representations.

sources.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

name: Vision-Language Projection
description: A learned projection maps visual representations produced by a vision encoder into the representation space expected by a language model, enabling multimodal token sequences.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual embeddings projected into language space

name: Audio Tokenization
description: Audio foundation models can represent speech and sound through spectrogram features, learned continuous embeddings, or discrete acoustic tokens produced by neural codecs.

sources.title: SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec

name: EnCodec
description: EnCodec is a neural audio codec that compresses audio into discrete codes, providing a representation that can be modeled by generative architectures.

name: Causal Language Modeling
description: Causal language modeling trains a model to predict the next token from preceding tokens, forming the dominant pretraining objective for decoder-only foundation models.

architecture.family: decoder-only Transformer or compatible sequence model

limitations: Potentially inefficient use of context compared with bidirectional objectives

sources.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

name: Masked Language Modeling
description: Masked Language Modeling hides selected tokens and trains the model to reconstruct them using surrounding context, enabling bidirectional representation learning.
limitations: Pretraining objective differs from natural generation

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

name: Span Corruption
description: Span corruption masks contiguous spans of input text and trains a sequence-to-sequence model to reconstruct the missing spans, providing a general text-to-text pretraining objective.
limitations: Encoder-decoder inference can be more expensive than decoder-only models for some workloads

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

name: Prefix Language Modeling
description: Prefix language modeling provides bidirectional attention within a prefix while using causal attention for subsequent tokens, combining aspects of encoder-style context understanding with autoregressive generation.
advantages: Strong conditioning on a known prefix

sources.title: Unified Language Model Pre-training for Natural Language Understanding and Generation

name: Contrastive Learning
description: Contrastive learning trains representations by bringing positive examples closer together while separating negative examples in embedding space.
limitations: Negative-sample design can strongly affect training

sources.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

name: CLIP-Style Image-Text Contrastive Learning
description: CLIP-style training jointly learns image and text representations by maximizing similarity between matching image-text pairs and minimizing similarity between mismatched pairs.
limitations: Performance depends on image-text data quality
Contrastive objective does not directly provide generative behavior

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

name: Supervised Fine-Tuning
description: Supervised fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model using curated input-output examples, often transforming a base model into an instruction-following model.
advantages: Can specialize models for specific domains
limitations: Quality depends heavily on demonstration data
May reduce generality if fine-tuning is narrow

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

name: RLHF
description: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback uses human preference judgments to train a reward model and then optimizes a language model toward preferred behavior.
advantages: Can improve helpfulness and instruction following

sources.title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback

name: Proximal Policy Optimization
description: PPO is a policy optimization algorithm that constrains policy updates to maintain stable learning, and became a common optimization method for RLHF pipelines.

name: Direct Preference Optimization
description: DPO directly optimizes a language model from preference pairs without requiring a separately trained reward model or an explicit reinforcement-learning loop.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

name: RLAIF
description: RLAIF replaces or supplements human preference labeling with judgments generated by an AI feedback model, allowing preference data to be produced at greater scale.
limitations: AI feedback may amplify model-specific errors

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

name: Group Relative Policy Optimization
description: GRPO is a policy optimization method that estimates relative advantages within groups of sampled responses and avoids requiring a separate value model, making it attractive for reinforcement learning of reasoning models.
advantages: Useful for reasoning tasks with verifiable rewards
limitations: Training dynamics depend strongly on sampling and reward design

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

name: Rejection Sampling
description: Rejection sampling generates multiple candidate outputs and retains only responses that satisfy a reward model, verifier, or quality criterion for subsequent training.
limitations: Potentially expensive because multiple samples are generated

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

name: Knowledge Distillation
description: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model to reproduce information contained in a larger teacher model, transferring behavior or representations while reducing deployment cost.
limitations: Student may fail to reproduce rare capabilities

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

name: Continued Pretraining
description: Continued pretraining extends the original pretraining process using additional domain-specific, language-specific, temporal, or higher-quality data before supervised or preference-based post-training.

sources.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks

name: Synthetic Data Training
description: Synthetic data training uses models, simulators, verifiers, or programmatic processes to generate additional training examples, often targeting specific capabilities or data distributions.
limitations: Distribution quality is difficult to guarantee
Synthetic data can reduce diversity if poorly constructed

sources.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions

name: Constitutional AI
description: Constitutional AI uses explicit principles to critique and revise model responses and can use AI-generated feedback instead of relying exclusively on human preference labels.

training.data: AI-generated critiques, revisions, and preference data

advantages: Reduces dependence on direct human preference labels
limitations: Quality depends on the chosen principles and evaluator
Does not eliminate alignment specification challenges

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

name: Parameter Scaling
description: Parameter scaling studies how increasing the number of learned parameters affects model capability, loss, compute requirements, memory consumption, and downstream performance.
advantages: Can improve performance with sufficient data and compute
limitations: Higher inference cost for dense models
Requires sufficient training data and compute

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

name: Neural Scaling Laws
description: Neural scaling laws describe empirical relationships between model loss and quantities such as model size, dataset size, and compute budget.
advantages: Provides empirical guidance for model design
limitations: Downstream capabilities may not scale identically to pretraining loss

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

name: Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling
description: Chinchilla demonstrated that many large language models were undertrained relative to their parameter count and showed that, under a fixed compute budget, model size and training data should be scaled together.
advantages: Changed how large language models were sized
limitations: Optimal ratios depend on assumptions and regime
Inference economics can favor different parameter/data choices

name: Data Scaling
description: Data scaling studies how increasing the amount, diversity, quality, and repetition characteristics of training data affects foundation-model performance.
advantages: Can improve capability without proportionally increasing parameter count
limitations: High-quality data is difficult to obtain
Data contamination and duplication can distort training

name: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Scaling
description: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts allows total parameter capacity to increase while activating only a subset of experts for each token, reducing the compute growth associated with dense parameter scaling.

scaling.effect: higher parameter capacity at lower per-token computation

advantages: Lower active computation than equivalent dense model

sources.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

name: Neural Network Quantization
description: Quantization reduces the numerical precision used to represent model weights, activations, or both, reducing memory usage and potentially improving inference efficiency.

scaling.effect: lower memory and potentially faster inference

sources.title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference

name: GPTQ
organization: IST Austria / ETH Zurich / Stanford / others
description: GPTQ performs approximate second-order post-training quantization of large language model weights, enabling highly compressed low-bit models without retraining the full network.

sources.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

name: AWQ
description: Activation-aware Weight Quantization protects salient weight channels identified through activation statistics while quantizing the majority of weights to low precision.

sources.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration

name: Neural Network Pruning
description: Pruning removes weights, neurons, heads, channels, or structured components judged to be unnecessary, reducing model size or computation.
advantages: Can preserve much of the original capability
limitations: Unstructured sparsity may not provide real hardware speedups

sources.title: Learning both Weights and Connections for Efficient Neural Networks

name: KV Cache
description: KV caching stores previously computed key and value representations during autoregressive generation so that they do not need to be recomputed for every newly generated token.

scaling.variable: cached sequence length × KV representation size

advantages: Avoids recomputation of previous K/V states
limitations: Can become the dominant inference-memory cost

sources.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

name: PagedAttention
description: PagedAttention manages KV-cache memory using non-contiguous blocks inspired by virtual memory systems, improving memory utilization and serving throughput for large language model inference.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

name: Speculative Decoding
description: Speculative decoding uses a smaller draft model to propose multiple tokens that are then verified in parallel by a larger target model, potentially increasing generation throughput without changing the target model's output distribution.

sources.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

name: Medusa
description: Medusa adds multiple decoding heads to a language model so that several future tokens can be predicted simultaneously and verified efficiently during generation.
advantages: Can accelerate decoding without a separate draft model

sources.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

name: Data Parallelism
description: Data parallelism replicates a model across devices and assigns different batches of training data to each replica, synchronizing gradients across workers.

scaling.effect: larger effective batch and parallel training

limitations: Each device must hold the model or relevant shard

name: Tensor Parallelism
description: Tensor parallelism partitions individual neural-network operations such as matrix multiplications across multiple devices so that a single layer is computed collaboratively.
advantages: Allows layers larger than one device's memory

sources.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

name: Pipeline Parallelism
description: Pipeline parallelism partitions a neural network into sequential stages placed on different devices and processes multiple microbatches concurrently through the pipeline.
advantages: Allows very large models to span devices

sources.title: PipeDream: Generalized Pipeline Parallelism for DNN Training

name: ZeRO
description: ZeRO partitions optimizer states, gradients, and optionally model parameters across data-parallel workers, substantially reducing redundant memory consumption.

sources.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

name: Expert Parallelism
description: Expert parallelism distributes different Mixture-of-Experts expert networks across devices and routes tokens between devices according to the gating decisions.

name: Recurrent Neural Network
description: Recurrent Neural Networks process sequences sequentially while maintaining a hidden state that carries information from previous positions.
advantages: Low memory footprint relative to full attention

name: Long Short-Term Memory
description: LSTM introduces gated memory cells that control information flow into, out of, and within a recurrent state, improving the ability to preserve information over long sequences.
advantages: Improved long-range memory over vanilla RNNs
Useful for sequential and streaming tasks
limitations: Less scalable for very large foundation models

name: Gated Recurrent Unit
description: GRU is a gated recurrent architecture that simplifies LSTM-style memory using update and reset gates.
advantages: Lower parameter count than many LSTM configurations
limitations: Limited scalability compared with highly parallel architectures

sources.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

name: State Space Model
description: State Space Models represent sequence dynamics through a latent state that evolves as inputs arrive, providing an alternative to explicit pairwise attention for long sequences.
advantages: Linear-time sequence processing in relevant formulations
limitations: Different optimization and representation tradeoffs from attention
State compression can limit direct access to all previous tokens

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

name: S4
description: S4 uses structured state space representations designed to efficiently model long-range dependencies while maintaining computationally efficient sequence processing.
limitations: Less widely deployed than Transformer architectures

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

name: S5
description: S5 simplifies multi-input multi-output state space modeling by using a single state space layer, reducing some of the complexity of earlier structured state space approaches.
advantages: Simpler architecture than some S4 formulations
limitations: Still less established than Transformer architectures

sources.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling

name: Mamba
description: Mamba introduces selective state space modeling in which input-dependent parameters control what information is propagated through the recurrent state, providing a linear-scaling alternative to attention for sequence modeling.
limitations: Does not provide direct pairwise token-to-token attention
Capability tradeoffs vary by task and model design
Architecture and kernels are more specialized

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

name: Mamba-2
description: Mamba-2 develops a structured state space approach that connects state space modeling and attention-like computation while improving hardware efficiency and simplifying the underlying formulation.

memory.complexity: linear-time sequence processing in the core formulation

limitations: Tradeoffs versus attention depend on workload

sources.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality

name: Mamba-3
description: Mamba-3 represents the subsequent evolution of the Mamba family, exploring improved state-space formulations and training mechanisms for language and long-context modeling.

name: RWKV
description: RWKV combines recurrent-style sequence processing with attention-inspired weighting, enabling efficient inference with constant-size recurrent state while retaining Transformer-like training characteristics.
limitations: Different scaling and capability tradeoffs from mainstream Transformers

sources.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

name: RetNet
description: RetNet introduces a retention mechanism designed to provide parallelizable training, recurrent inference, and efficient sequence computation as alternatives to standard Transformer attention.
limitations: Tradeoffs depend on task and implementation

sources.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

name: Hyena
description: Hyena replaces explicit quadratic attention with long convolutions and element-wise gating, providing a subquadratic alternative for long-context sequence modeling.

sources.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models

name: Linear Attention
description: Linear attention reformulates attention computation so that the sequence-length dependence can be reduced from quadratic to linear under specific kernel or feature-map formulations.

memory.complexity: linear in sequence length under applicable formulations

limitations: Approximation or reformulation can alter attention behavior

sources.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention

name: xLSTM
description: xLSTM revisits recurrent memory using exponential gating and new scalar and matrix memory variants designed to improve scalability and long-range sequence modeling.
limitations: Deployment and scaling evidence is smaller than Transformer ecosystem

name: Hybrid Attention-State Space Architecture
description: Hybrid architectures combine attention layers with state-space or recurrent layers, attempting to capture both direct token-to-token interactions and efficient long-range state propagation.
advantages: Can reduce dependence on full attention

name: Jamba
description: Jamba combines Transformer attention, Mamba-style state space layers, and Mixture-of-Experts components in a hybrid architecture designed for efficient long-context language modeling.

name: Dual-Encoder Multimodal Architecture
description: A dual-encoder architecture independently encodes two modalities into compatible representation spaces and aligns them using a similarity or contrastive objective.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: independent encoding followed by representation alignment

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

name: CLIP
description: CLIP jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder to produce aligned representations using large-scale image-text contrastive learning.
limitations: Not a general-purpose multimodal conversational model

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

name: SigLIP
description: SigLIP is a vision-language dual encoder that replaces CLIP's softmax contrastive objective with a pairwise sigmoid loss for image-text alignment.
advantages: Useful as a vision encoder for multimodal models
limitations: Not inherently a general-purpose conversational generator

sources.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

name: Cross-Attention Multimodal Fusion
description: Cross-attention fusion allows representations from one modality to attend to representations from another modality, enabling token-level or feature-level multimodal interaction.

fusion.mechanism: queries from one modality attend to keys and values from another

limitations: Cross-attention memory grows with multimodal sequence sizes

name: Flamingo
description: Flamingo connects a pretrained vision encoder to a pretrained language model through specialized cross-attention layers, enabling few-shot multimodal generation.
advantages: Supports interleaved visual and textual inputs

sources.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

name: BLIP-2
description: BLIP-2 connects frozen vision and language models through a lightweight Querying Transformer that learns to extract visual information useful for language generation.
advantages: Efficient reuse of frozen pretrained components
Strong visual question answering and image understanding
limitations: Depends on quality of pretrained components

sources.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

name: Vision-Language Projection
description: A modality projector maps representations produced by a vision encoder into the representation space expected by a language model.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual tokens projected into language-model space

advantages: Easy integration with pretrained language models
limitations: Projection can create an information bottleneck

name: LLaVA
organization: University of Wisconsin–Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University
description: LLaVA connects a pretrained vision encoder to a large language model through a learned projection layer, enabling visual instruction following and multimodal conversation.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual tokens inserted into language sequence

advantages: Easy adaptation of existing language models
limitations: Vision information must pass through a projector
Performance depends on vision encoder and language model

name: PaliGemma
description: PaliGemma combines a SigLIP vision encoder with a Gemma language model in a compact vision-language architecture designed for image understanding and generation tasks.
limitations: Architecture has a relatively constrained multimodal interface
Capability depends on model scale and adaptation

name: Qwen-VL
description: Qwen-VL integrates visual representations with the Qwen language-model family to support image understanding, visual question answering, and multimodal generation.
limitations: Exact components should be recorded per release

sources.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond

name: InternVL
description: InternVL is a vision-language model family that combines large-scale visual encoders with language models and progressively improves visual understanding, resolution handling, and multimodal instruction following.
limitations: High-resolution processing can increase computational cost

sources.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks

name: IDEFICS
description: IDEFICS is an open vision-language model family designed for image-text understanding and generation using pretrained vision and language components.
limitations: Earlier generation compared with newer VLMs
Performance varies significantly by model version

sources.title: IDEFICS: An Open Reproduction of Flamingo

name: KOSMOS
description: KOSMOS explores a general multimodal language modeling framework capable of grounding language in visual information and supporting tasks such as image understanding and multimodal interaction.

fusion.mechanism: visual embeddings integrated into language sequence

advantages: Grounding of language in visual context
limitations: Earlier architecture relative to current VLM systems

sources.title: Language Is Not All You Need: Aligning Perception with Language Models

name: Early Multimodal Token Fusion
description: Early multimodal fusion represents multiple modalities as tokens or token-like representations that can be processed jointly by a shared autoregressive Transformer.

name: Chameleon
description: Chameleon is a mixed-modal early-fusion foundation model that processes interleaved text and image tokens within a shared autoregressive Transformer framework.

name: Janus
description: Janus explores unified multimodal understanding and generation while decoupling visual encoding strategies for the two tasks, allowing the system to handle both perception and image generation.

architecture.family: unified multimodal model with decoupled visual pathways
architecture.sequenceStrategy: unified language modeling with decoupled visual encoding

advantages: Combines multimodal understanding and image generation
Explores unified architecture with task-specific visual representations

sources.title: Janus: Decoupling Visual Encoding for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation

name: Word-Level Tokenization
description: Word-level tokenization represents text primarily as complete words or whitespace-delimited units. It is conceptually simple but produces very large vocabularies and struggles with rare, unseen, and morphologically complex words.

efficiency.sequenceLength: shorter than subword tokenization for many texts

name: Character-Level Representation
description: Character-level representation treats individual characters as the basic sequence units, avoiding vocabulary-level unknown words at the cost of much longer sequences.

representation.unknownToken: often unnecessary for known character sets

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but high sequence-processing cost

advantages: Handles arbitrary words through character composition
limitations: Higher computational cost for long text

name: Byte Pair Encoding
description: Byte Pair Encoding builds a subword vocabulary by iteratively merging frequently occurring symbol pairs. In neural language modeling it provides a compromise between character-level flexibility and word-level efficiency.
advantages: Balances vocabulary size and sequence length
limitations: Can be inefficient for some languages and domains

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

name: WordPiece
description: WordPiece represents text using a learned vocabulary of subword units and was widely used in Transformer encoder models such as BERT.
advantages: Handles unknown and rare words better than word-level tokenization
Effective for multilingual and general NLP settings
limitations: Can produce inefficient sequences for some languages

name: SentencePiece
description: SentencePiece is a language-independent tokenization framework that learns subword segmentation directly from raw text without requiring whitespace-based preprocessing.
limitations: Tokenizer behavior depends on training configuration
Segmentation can differ substantially across model families

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing

name: Unigram Language Model Tokenization
description: Unigram tokenization starts from a large candidate vocabulary and iteratively removes pieces according to a probabilistic language-model objective, selecting segmentations based on likelihood.
advantages: Multiple possible segmentations can be modeled

sources.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates

name: Byte-Level BPE
description: Byte-level BPE applies BPE-style merging over byte representations, allowing arbitrary text and Unicode content to be represented without relying on a fixed character vocabulary.

representation.unknownToken: typically unnecessary for arbitrary byte sequences

advantages: Works across languages and unusual strings
limitations: Some languages can require many tokens
Token efficiency depends strongly on vocabulary and corpus

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

name: Byte-Level Representation
description: Byte-level representation processes raw byte sequences directly or with minimal learned segmentation, providing universal coverage of textual data while potentially increasing sequence length.

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but potentially high sequence-processing cost

name: Vision Patch Tokenization
description: Vision patch tokenization divides an image into fixed-size or structured patches and maps each patch to an embedding that can be processed as a sequence of visual tokens.

efficiency.sequenceLength: proportional to image area and inverse patch area

advantages: Simple conversion of images into Transformer-compatible sequences
limitations: Fixed patch size may lose fine-grained information

sources.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

name: Discrete Image Tokenization
description: Discrete image tokenization converts continuous visual information into a sequence of discrete codebook indices, allowing image content to be modeled using token-prediction architectures.
advantages: Allows image generation using token prediction

name: Audio Tokenization
description: Audio tokenization converts speech, music, or general audio into compact continuous or discrete representations that can be processed by sequence models.

representation.unit: audio frame or discrete codec code

efficiency.sequenceLength: depends on frame rate and compression

advantages: Can support speech generation and understanding
limitations: Temporal sequences can remain very long

name: EnCodec
description: EnCodec is a neural audio codec that compresses audio into discrete latent representations using an encoder, quantization mechanism, and decoder.
advantages: Discrete representations suitable for generative modeling
limitations: Multiple codebooks can increase sequence complexity

name: Speech Tokenization
description: Speech tokenization represents spoken language as learned acoustic, phonetic, semantic, or codec units that can be modeled by sequence architectures.
advantages: Allows speech to be modeled as discrete sequences
Can unify speech and language modeling
limitations: Speech contains information at multiple timescales

name: Video Tokenization
description: Video tokenization converts spatial and temporal visual information into sequences of visual tokens representing frames, patches, or compressed spatiotemporal units.

efficiency.sequenceLength: grows with spatial and temporal resolution

name: Unified Multimodal Token Space
description: A unified multimodal token space represents multiple modalities using compatible token-like representations that can be processed within a common sequence-modeling framework.

efficiency.memory: depends on total multimodal token count

limitations: Token counts can become extremely large
Different modalities have very different information densities

name: Tokenizer-Free Modeling
description: Tokenizer-free models process byte-level or character-level representations directly rather than relying on a conventional learned subword tokenizer, aiming to simplify multilingual and arbitrary-text processing.

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but potentially higher sequence-processing cost

advantages: Potentially better handling of unusual strings
limitations: Higher compute requirements for equivalent text
Requires architectures optimized for long sequences

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

name: ByT5
description: ByT5 is a tokenizer-free sequence-to-sequence Transformer that operates directly on UTF-8 byte sequences rather than conventional subword tokens.

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

name: Foundation Model Evaluation Taxonomy
description: A capability-oriented framework for evaluating foundation models across knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, coding, instruction following, multilingual ability, multimodal understanding, long-context processing, safety, factuality, tool use, and agentic performance.
limitations: Poor correlation with some real-world tasks

name: MMLU
description: Massive Multitask Language Understanding evaluates language models across a broad collection of academic and professional subjects using multiple-choice questions.
limitations: Does not fully measure open-ended reasoning

name: MMLU-Pro
description: MMLU-Pro extends the original MMLU evaluation with more challenging questions and a stronger emphasis on reasoning.
advantages: More challenging than many original MMLU questions
Reduced dependence on simple answer selection

sources.title: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark

name: GPQA
description: GPQA evaluates advanced scientific reasoning using difficult questions designed to be resistant to straightforward web search and accessible primarily to domain experts.

sources.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark

name: GSM8K
description: GSM8K evaluates multi-step mathematical reasoning using grade-school word problems.

sources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems

name: AIME
description: The American Invitational Mathematics Examination provides difficult competition mathematics problems that are increasingly used as evaluations of advanced mathematical reasoning in AI systems.
limitations: Not designed specifically as an AI benchmark
Potential exposure through training or public solutions

name: HumanEval
description: HumanEval evaluates code-generation models using programming problems with function signatures and hidden tests.
advantages: More meaningful than text similarity metrics
limitations: Does not fully represent software engineering

sources.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

name: SWE-bench
description: SWE-bench evaluates whether language models can resolve real GitHub issues by modifying repositories and producing patches that satisfy tests.
limitations: Environment and setup can affect results

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?

name: IFEval
description: IFEval evaluates whether language models follow verifiable natural-language instructions containing explicit constraints.
limitations: Does not fully capture subjective instruction quality

sources.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models

name: BIG-Bench Hard
description: BIG-Bench Hard is a curated subset of challenging BIG-bench tasks selected for their difficulty for language models and their relevance to reasoning capabilities.

sources.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models

name: ARC
description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge evaluates scientific question answering using grade-school science questions divided into standard and challenge sets.
advantages: Challenge subset targets more difficult questions

sources.title: Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge

name: HellaSwag
description: HellaSwag evaluates commonsense reasoning by asking models to select plausible continuations of scenarios.
advantages: Designed to challenge strong language models

sources.title: HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?

name: TruthfulQA
description: TruthfulQA evaluates whether language models produce truthful answers to questions designed to expose common misconceptions and false beliefs.
limitations: Truthfulness is difficult to reduce to a single metric
Evaluation can depend on reference judgments
Does not directly measure grounding against provided evidence

sources.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods

name: MMMU
description: MMMU evaluates multimodal reasoning across university-level subjects using questions that require understanding images, diagrams, charts, and text.
limitations: Does not cover all real-world multimodal tasks

sources.title: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI

name: MathVista
description: MathVista evaluates mathematical reasoning involving visual information such as charts, diagrams, geometry, and scientific figures.

sources.title: MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts

name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA evaluates visual question answering over document images, requiring models to combine document layout, text recognition, and semantic understanding.

sources.title: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images

name: LongBench
description: LongBench evaluates language models across diverse tasks requiring understanding and reasoning over long contexts.
advantages: Evaluates long-context behavior across multiple tasks
More informative than context-window size alone
limitations: Long-context benchmark performance depends on task distribution
Does not establish reliable performance at every advertised context length

sources.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding

name: RULER
description: RULER evaluates long-context capabilities using controlled tasks designed to measure retrieval, reasoning, and manipulation of information across long sequences.
advantages: Can probe degradation as context grows
limitations: Synthetic tasks may not fully represent real workloads
Benchmark performance can differ from natural-document retrieval

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

name: Video-MME
description: Video-MME evaluates multimodal models on video understanding across different video durations and domains.
advantages: More representative of video tasks than image-only benchmarks

sources.title: Video-MME: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multi-modal Large Language Models in Video Analysis

name: Benchmark Contamination
description: Benchmark contamination occurs when evaluation examples or closely related information are present in a model's training data, potentially inflating reported performance.
limitations: Semantic contamination can occur without exact string overlap

name: Human Evaluation
description: Human evaluation uses human judgments to assess qualities that automated metrics may not reliably capture, including helpfulness, preference, factuality, style, and overall response quality.

name: LLM-as-a-Judge
description: LLM-as-a-Judge uses a language model to evaluate or rank outputs produced by other models according to a rubric or comparison protocol.
advantages: Scales evaluation more cheaply than human annotation
limitations: Potential agreement with its own model family

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena

name: Arena-Style Pairwise Evaluation
description: Arena-style evaluation compares model outputs pairwise, often using anonymous human preferences, and aggregates results into a ranking or rating system.
limitations: Preference is not identical to correctness

name: Agent Evaluation
description: Agent evaluation measures whether models can plan, use tools, interact with environments, maintain state, recover from errors, and complete multi-step tasks.
limitations: Small implementation differences can alter results

name: Foundation Model Evaluation Reliability
description: Evaluation reliability concerns whether benchmark results accurately measure the capability they claim to measure and whether scores generalize across prompts, datasets, languages, evaluators, and real-world tasks.

name: Foundation Model Pretraining
description: Pretraining learns general-purpose representations or generative capabilities from large-scale datasets before task-specific adaptation or post-training.
advantages: Supports transfer to many downstream tasks
Can exploit very large heterogeneous datasets
limitations: Training-data composition can introduce unwanted biases

name: Causal Language Modeling
description: Causal language modeling trains a model to predict the next token conditioned on preceding tokens, typically using a causal attention mask.
advantages: Scales effectively with large language models
limitations: Training requires processing long token sequences
Standard causal attention does not directly see future tokens

name: Masked Language Modeling
description: Masked language modeling trains an encoder-style model to reconstruct tokens that have been masked or corrupted within an input sequence.
advantages: Each masked token can use information from both sides
limitations: Pretraining corruption differs from ordinary generation

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

name: Sequence-to-Sequence Training
description: Sequence-to-sequence training learns to transform an input sequence into an output sequence, typically using an encoder to represent the input and a decoder to generate the target.
advantages: Natural for translation and transformation tasks
limitations: More architectural components than decoder-only models

name: Training Data Filtering
description: Data filtering removes low-quality, irrelevant, duplicated, unsafe, or otherwise undesirable examples before or during foundation-model training.
limitations: Aggressive filtering can remove useful information
Classifier errors can bias the corpus
Exact filtering pipelines are often proprietary

name: Training Data Deduplication
description: Data deduplication identifies and removes exact or near-duplicate examples from training corpora to reduce redundancy, improve effective data diversity, and mitigate memorization and contamination risks.
limitations: Over-deduplication can remove legitimate related examples

name: Training Data Mixture
description: A training data mixture defines the relative composition of different domains, sources, languages, modalities, or quality levels used during model training.
importance: Influences model capabilities
Influences domain specialization
Influences multilingual performance
Influences downstream behavior
limitations: Mixture percentages alone do not capture data quality
Repeated training or resampling complicates interpretation

name: Continued Pretraining
description: Continued pretraining further trains an existing pretrained model on additional data, often to improve domain, language, modality, or temporal specialization while retaining much of the original model's capabilities.
advantages: Preserves pretrained capabilities more readily than full retraining
limitations: May not fully update parametric knowledge

name: Supervised Fine-Tuning
description: Supervised fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model using labeled input-output examples, commonly instruction-response pairs for language models.
advantages: Can specialize models for specific tasks
limitations: Does not directly optimize human preferences

name: Instruction Tuning
description: Instruction tuning trains pretrained models on diverse task instructions and demonstrations so they learn to interpret natural-language requests and produce task-appropriate responses.
advantages: Makes pretrained models easier to interact with
Can consolidate many tasks into one model

name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
description: RLHF uses human preference judgments to train a reward model or otherwise derive a preference signal that is then used to optimize the language model.
advantages: Supports optimization of qualities difficult to specify with supervised labels
limitations: Human preference may not equal factual correctness

name: Reward Modeling
description: Reward modeling learns a model that assigns scores or preferences to outputs based on human or other preference signals.
advantages: Provides a scalable learned preference signal
limitations: Reward scores may not correspond to actual task success

name: Direct Preference Optimization
description: Direct Preference Optimization trains a language model directly from preference pairs without requiring a separately trained reward model and explicit reinforcement-learning loop.
advantages: Does not require a separate reward-model training stage
limitations: Not a universal replacement for reinforcement learning

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

name: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback
description: RLAIF uses AI-generated evaluations or preferences as a major source of feedback for preference optimization or reinforcement learning.
advantages: Reduces reliance on large-scale human labeling
Useful for safety and behavioral alignment
limitations: AI judgments may not match human preferences

name: Constitutional AI
description: Constitutional AI uses explicit principles or a constitution to guide model self-critique, revision, and preference generation, reducing dependence on direct human preference labeling for some stages.
advantages: Can reduce some forms of human annotation
limitations: AI-generated feedback can propagate model biases
Does not eliminate the need for evaluation

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

name: Group Relative Policy Optimization
description: GRPO is a reinforcement-learning method that estimates relative advantages among multiple sampled responses from a group, reducing reliance on a separate value model.
advantages: Can reduce memory associated with separate value models
limitations: Sampling multiple responses increases training cost
Optimization remains sensitive to reward design

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

name: Verifiable Reward Training
description: Verifiable reward training optimizes models using rewards that can be automatically checked against objective criteria such as mathematical answers, executable code, formal proofs, or game outcomes.
advantages: Less dependence on subjective human preferences
limitations: Only works when reliable verification exists
Reward may capture correctness without capturing quality
Poorly designed verifiers can be exploited

name: Synthetic Training Data
description: Synthetic training data consists of examples generated or transformed by models, simulations, procedural systems, or other automated processes for use in training foundation models.
advantages: Can generate difficult or rare examples
limitations: Model collapse risks under careless recursive training

name: Knowledge Distillation
description: Knowledge distillation trains a student model to reproduce or approximate information contained in a larger teacher model or ensemble.
advantages: Can transfer capabilities to smaller models
limitations: Student may not reproduce all teacher capabilities
Distillation quality depends on data and objective

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

name: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model while updating only a small subset of parameters or adding trainable parameters rather than updating the full model.
advantages: Multiple task-specific adapters can share one base model
limitations: May reduce adaptation capacity for some tasks
Quality depends on method and rank/configuration

name: LoRA
description: LoRA adapts a pretrained neural network by freezing the original weights and learning low-rank update matrices.
limitations: Rank selection affects quality and cost
Not always equivalent to full fine-tuning

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

name: QLoRA
description: QLoRA combines low-rank adaptation with quantized base-model weights to substantially reduce memory requirements during fine-tuning.
advantages: Enables fine-tuning larger models on more accessible hardware
limitations: Hardware and implementation details affect performance

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

name: Training Compute
description: Training compute describes the computational resources required to optimize a foundation model, including accelerator count, training duration, numerical precision, communication overhead, and total floating-point operations.
advantages: Provides a basis for understanding training cost
Connects model scale with compute requirements
limitations: FLOPs alone do not capture actual cost

name: Scaling Laws
description: Scaling laws describe empirical relationships between model performance or loss and factors such as parameter count, training data, and compute.
principle: Model loss often follows predictable approximate power-law relationships over substantial ranges of scale.
advantages: Helps predict performance at larger scales
Provides a quantitative framework for model development
limitations: Scaling relationships are empirical rather than universal laws
Architecture changes can alter scaling behavior
Extrapolation can fail outside observed regimes

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

name: Kaplan Scaling Laws
description: The Kaplan scaling-law framework demonstrated predictable power-law relationships between language-model loss and model size, dataset size, and compute over studied regimes.
principle: Performance improves predictably with scale under fixed training and architectural assumptions.
importance: Established quantitative scaling analysis for language models
Influenced large-model training strategies
Provided a basis for compute-performance forecasting
limitations: Scaling depends on the training regime and data assumptions

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

name: Chinchilla Scaling
description: Chinchilla scaling demonstrated that, for a fixed training-compute budget under the studied regime, many large language models were undertrained and that increasing training tokens alongside model size could produce better compute-optimal models.
principle: Model parameters and training tokens should be scaled together rather than maximizing parameter count alone.
importance: Changed how compute-optimal language-model training was understood
Highlighted the importance of training-token budgets
Influenced subsequent model scaling strategies
limitations: The exact optimal relationship depends on assumptions
Data quality and architecture affect the tradeoff
Training compute is only one dimension of practical cost

name: Compute-Optimal Training
description: Compute-optimal training seeks the model size and training-data allocation that maximize model quality under a fixed computational budget.
objective: maximize model quality under a fixed compute budget
advantages: Improves use of limited training compute
Separates parameter scaling from training-token scaling
limitations: Optimality depends on the chosen metric
Inference economics may favor a different training point

name: Parameter Scaling
description: Parameter scaling increases the number of learned model parameters to increase representational capacity, subject to data and compute constraints.
benefits: Potentially improved capability with sufficient data and compute
costs: Higher inference cost for dense models
limitations: More parameters do not automatically produce better models
Undertraining can reduce the value of additional parameters
Inference cost becomes important at deployment

name: Data Scaling
description: Data scaling increases the quantity and diversity of training examples or tokens available to a model.
benefits: Improves learning when additional high-quality data is useful
Can reduce undertraining of large models
limitations: Repeated data can reduce effective diversity
Additional low-quality data may provide limited benefit

name: Mixture-of-Experts Compute Efficiency
description: Mixture-of-Experts architectures increase total parameter capacity while activating only a subset of experts for each token or input.
benefits: Lower active compute than an equivalent fully dense model in some regimes
Supports scaling model capacity without proportional active computation

name: Active vs Total Parameters
description: Total parameters describe the full stored model capacity, while active parameters describe the parameters actually involved in computing a particular token or input, especially in sparse architectures such as MoE models.
importance: Prevents misleading comparisons between dense and sparse models
Helps estimate compute requirements
Clarifies model capacity versus per-token computation

name: Sparse Computation
description: Sparse computation reduces the amount of computation performed for a given input by activating only selected parameters, connections, tokens, or operations.
benefits: Potentially larger model capacity at similar compute
limitations: Communication overhead may offset theoretical savings

name: Distillation for Inference Efficiency
description: Distillation transfers capabilities from a larger teacher model into a smaller student model to reduce inference cost while attempting to preserve useful behavior.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

name: Model Quantization
description: Quantization represents model weights, activations, or other numerical values using lower-precision representations to reduce memory and computational requirements.
benefits: Enables larger models on constrained hardware
limitations: Different quantization methods have different quality-cost tradeoffs

name: Post-Training Quantization
description: Post-training quantization converts an already trained model to lower numerical precision without requiring full retraining.
limitations: Very low precision can be challenging

name: GPTQ
description: GPTQ is a post-training weight-quantization method designed to compress large Transformer models to low-bit precision while attempting to preserve model quality.

sources.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

name: AWQ
description: AWQ is a weight-quantization method that uses activation information to identify important weights and protect them during low-bit quantization.
principle: Protect salient weights based on activation behavior.

sources.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration

name: Key-Value Cache
description: The key-value cache stores previously computed attention keys and values during autoregressive generation so they do not need to be recomputed for every newly generated token.
costs: Large batch sizes increase cache requirements

name: Grouped Query Attention for Inference Efficiency
description: Grouped Query Attention reduces key-value cache size by sharing key and value heads across groups of query heads.
benefits: Retains more query-head capacity than single-KV-head designs
tradeoffs: Potential quality differences compared with full multi-head attention

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints

name: Multi-Query Attention
description: Multi-Query Attention uses many query heads but shares a single key and value head across them, substantially reducing KV-cache memory during autoregressive inference.
limitations: Less expressive key-value representation than full multi-head attention

sources.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

name: Multi-head Latent Attention
description: Multi-head Latent Attention compresses key-value information into a lower-dimensional latent representation to reduce inference memory while retaining multi-head attention behavior.
benefits: Retains richer attention structure than simple shared KV heads

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong Mixture-of-Experts Language Model

name: Speculative Decoding
description: Speculative decoding uses a smaller draft model or auxiliary mechanism to propose multiple tokens that a larger target model verifies in parallel.
benefits: Preserves target-model output distribution under appropriate algorithms
Reduces the number of sequential target-model decoding steps
limitations: Speedup depends on draft acceptance rate
Requires suitable draft or prediction mechanism

sources.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling

name: Continuous Batching
description: Continuous batching dynamically adds and removes generation requests from an active batch rather than waiting for all requests in a static batch to finish.
benefits: Better handling of requests with different sequence lengths

name: Prefix Caching
description: Prefix caching reuses previously computed attention states for shared prompt prefixes across multiple requests.
limitations: Cache memory requirements can be substantial

name: Test-Time Compute Scaling
description: Test-time compute scaling increases the amount of computation performed after a prompt is received, allowing a model to spend additional computation on reasoning, sampling, verification, search, or candidate selection.
benefits: Can improve performance without increasing base-model parameter count
Allows adaptive computation based on task difficulty

name: Best-of-N Sampling
description: Best-of-N sampling generates multiple candidate responses and selects the highest-scoring candidate according to a reward model, verifier, judge, or other evaluation mechanism.
costs: Selection quality depends on evaluator quality

name: Inference Throughput vs Latency
description: Inference serving involves a tradeoff between latency for individual requests and throughput across many concurrent requests.

name: Scaling–Efficiency Tradeoff
description: Foundation-model design requires balancing capability, training compute, inference cost, memory, latency, throughput, and data requirements rather than maximizing model size alone.
principle: The best model is workload-dependent rather than universally defined by parameter count.

name: Context Window
description: The context window is the amount of input and previously generated information that a model can process within a single inference context.
importance: Determines how much information can be presented to the model at once
Affects long-document processing
Affects conversational memory
Affects retrieval and agent workflows
limitations: A larger context window does not guarantee effective use of all information
Long contexts increase memory and computation requirements
Information can be lost or underweighted within long contexts

name: Long-Context Modeling
description: Long-context modeling enables foundation models to process substantially longer sequences than conventional language models while attempting to preserve useful information across the context.
limitations: Effective context utilization can be lower than advertised context length
Attention and KV-cache costs can become significant

name: Rotary Position Embedding
description: Rotary Position Embedding encodes token positions by rotating query and key representations according to position-dependent frequencies.
advantages: Integrates positional information directly into attention
Works effectively in Transformer language models
limitations: Extrapolation beyond the training context can be difficult
Long-context extension often requires additional techniques

sources.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding

name: ALiBi
description: Attention with Linear Biases adds position-dependent linear biases to attention scores instead of injecting positional embeddings into token representations.
advantages: Can support length extrapolation in some settings
limitations: Performance depends on architecture and training regime
Not universally superior to rotary position methods

sources.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation

name: YaRN
description: YaRN is a method for extending the effective context length of models using improved rotary-position scaling and attention-temperature adjustments.
advantages: Can require substantially less additional training than training a model from scratch at the target context length
limitations: Long-context quality depends on the original model
Extension does not guarantee uniform information retrieval across the entire context

sources.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

name: Sliding Window Attention
description: Sliding Window Attention restricts each token's attention to a local neighborhood rather than the complete sequence, reducing attention computation for long sequences.

mechanism.complexity: approximately linear in sequence length for fixed window size

limitations: Information may need to propagate across multiple layers

name: Sparse Attention
description: Sparse attention restricts attention connections so that each token attends to only a subset of other positions, reducing the computational cost of full attention.
limitations: Sparse patterns may miss important dependencies

name: Linear Attention
description: Linear attention methods reformulate attention so sequence processing can scale approximately linearly with sequence length under specific kernel or recurrent formulations.
advantages: Lower memory requirements for long sequences
limitations: Approximation or reformulation may change attention behavior
Quality can differ substantially from full attention

name: Recurrent Memory
description: Recurrent memory mechanisms maintain a compressed or recurrent state across sequence segments so information can persist without placing the entire history into the active attention context.
advantages: Supports sequences longer than the immediate attention window
limitations: Memory state may become difficult to interpret
Training and inference behavior depend on architecture

name: State-Space Memory
description: State-space models process sequences through evolving latent states, providing an alternative to conventional full self-attention for long-sequence modeling.
advantages: Lower asymptotic sequence complexity in relevant formulations
limitations: Different inductive biases from full attention

name: External Memory
description: External memory systems store information outside the model's immediate context and retrieve relevant information when required.
advantages: Can store information beyond the context window
Can update information without retraining model weights
limitations: Retrieved information can be incomplete or incorrect

name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a generative model with an external retrieval system so relevant information can be supplied to the model at inference time.
advantages: Can reduce dependence on parametric memory
Supports knowledge updates without full model retraining
limitations: Correct retrieval does not guarantee faithful generation
System quality depends on indexing and ranking

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

name: Dense Retrieval
description: Dense retrieval represents queries and documents as continuous vectors and retrieves items based on vector similarity.
advantages: Efficient retrieval over large collections with suitable indexes
Less dependent on exact lexical overlap
limitations: Fine-grained exact matching can be difficult
